title: Unique Paths
keyIdea: Every path from top-left to bottom-right takes exactly n − 1 rights and m − 1 downs, m + n − 2 steps in all. Paths differ only in which of those steps are downs, so the answer is C(m + n − 2, m − 1). The DP view gives the same number: paths(r, c) = paths from the cell below + paths from the cell to the right.

approaches.name: Memoization from the start
approaches.idea: count(r, c) = count(r + 1, c) + count(r, c + 1); a cell on the last row or last column has exactly 1 path. Save each answer in dp.
approaches.why: Each of the m × n cells is solved once with O(1) work; dp table plus a stack up to m + n deep.

approaches.name: Memoization from the end
approaches.idea: Same recurrence the other way round: count(r, c) = count(r − 1, c) + count(r, c − 1) on 1-based sizes; row 1 or column 1 has 1 path.
approaches.why: Same m × n states; the dp is (m + 1) × (n + 1) because it is 1-based.

approaches.name: Tabulation
approaches.idea: Fill dp with 1s (first row and column have one path), then dp[i][j] = dp[i − 1][j] + dp[i][j − 1]. Answer dp[m − 1][n − 1].
approaches.why: Two nested loops over the grid; the whole table is kept. One row of size n would be enough.

approaches.name: Combinatorics
approaches.idea: Your active code: N = m + n − 2 steps, r = m − 1 of them down, answer C(N, r) built as res = res × (N − r + i) / i for i = 1..r.
approaches.why: One loop of m − 1 steps and three variables. After step i, res = C(N − r + i, i), so each division is exact.

quiz.q: How many steps does every path take in an m × n grid?
options: m + n − 2: n − 1 rights and m − 1 downs

quiz.q: Why is the answer C(m + n − 2, m − 1)?
options: A path is fixed once you choose which m − 1 of the steps are downs
There are m − 1 rows to skip
It is the number of cells on the diagonal

quiz.q: In res = res * (N - r + i) / i, why multiply before dividing?
options: After each step res is C(N − r + i, i), a whole number, so dividing last is exact

quiz.q: In the DP, why is every cell in the first row and first column 1?
options: You can only reach them by going straight right or straight down
They are the base of the recursion stack
